title: Student loans in Germany for international students
description: Which loans international students can get in Germany, which need no guarantor, how to apply and which alternatives exist when a loan is not the answer.
html:
Because tuition at public universities is close to zero, most students in Germany borrow little or nothing. But living costs of about €1,000 a month add up, and a loan can bridge a gap. The options for international students are narrower than for Germans, and it pays to know which ones are realistic.

Can international students borrow at all?

Yes, but with conditions. The state development bank's student loan is open to EU citizens and to non-EU students who have lived in Germany for some years or are enrolled in a programme with a German partner. The federal education loan is open to advanced students of all nationalities under certain conditions. Commercial banks generally require a German income or a guarantor.

Loans without a guarantor

A few international lenders specialise in loans for students at selected universities and assess future earning potential instead of requiring collateral. Interest rates are higher than domestic student loans, and the list of eligible programmes is limited, so check before you plan around one.

The main options

  • State student loan: up to €650 a month for up to 14 semesters at a moderate interest rate; eligibility depends on nationality and residence history.
  • Federal education loan: up to €300 a month for advanced students, low interest, open to more nationalities.
  • Income-share and international lenders: no guarantor, higher cost, limited to partner universities.
  • Loans from your home country: many countries offer education loans for study abroad, sometimes with government backing; conditions vary widely.

How to apply

Check eligibility on the lender's site, gather your admission letter, passport, residence permit or visa and proof of enrolment, submit the application online, and expect a decision within two to six weeks. Disbursement usually starts after enrolment, so a loan cannot replace the Blocked Account for the visa.

Alternatives

Part-time work of up to 20 hours a week during term covers a significant share of costs. Scholarships, even partial ones, reduce what you need to borrow. Choosing a cheaper city can save €300 a month, which over a degree is more than most loans.
